name: Nintendo Wii family
summary: Explore Nintendo Wii family hardware and the model-dependent routes into homebrew: Wilbrand on SD-capable consoles and BlueBomb on the Wii mini, all ending at the HackMii installer.

specs.memory: 88 MB total (24 MB main + 64 MB graphics)
specs.storage: 512 MB internal flash; SD card for expansion
specs.media: Wii 12 cm optical discs; GameCube 8 cm discs on the original model
specs.display: Up to 480p via component or AV

variants.notes: Model code RVL-001. GameCube controller and memory-card ports. SD and USB exploit path (Wilbrand).
Model code RVL-101. Horizontal-only case; no GameCube ports. SD and USB exploit path (Wilbrand).

variants.storage: 512 MB internal flash; USB only (no SD slot)
variants.notes: Model code RVL-201. No GameCube ports and no SD slot. Bluetooth exploit (BlueBomb) is the only entry.

homebrew.name: Wilbrand
homebrew.summary: An SD-card exploit for Wii Menu 4.3 that leads to the HackMii installer. Requires the SD slot, so it does not apply to the Wii mini.

compatibility.note: The guide marks the Wii and Family Edition as SD and USB capable; Wilbrand is the SD route for 4.3.

requirements: A Wii or Wii Family Edition with an SD slot.
An SD card prepared with Wilbrand.
A computer to run the exploit tool.
warnings: The Wii mini has no SD slot, so Wilbrand does not apply to it.

homebrew.name: BlueBomb
homebrew.summary: A Bluetooth exploit used for the Wii mini and usable on original Wiis. The console must be close to the computer running it.

compatibility.note: BlueBomb is the only entry for the Wii mini and also works on original Wiis; it needs Bluetooth proximity.

requirements: A Bluetooth adapter on the computer running the exploit.
The console within Bluetooth range.
Wii Menu 4.3 on the console.
warnings: BlueBomb is the only Wii mini entry; do not plan a mini mod around a disc or SD exploit.

homebrew.name: HackMii installer
homebrew.summary: The shared installer that all Wii and Wii mini routes end at. It installs the Homebrew Channel and, where supported, BootMii.

compatibility.note: Every Wii and Wii mini route ends at the HackMii installer, which checks the console before writing.

requirements: A working Wilbrand or BlueBomb entry point.
An SD card or USB drive as required by the route.
warnings: The installer decides whether BootMii-boot2 is available on a given revision.

homebrew.name: Homebrew Channel
homebrew.summary: The launcher installed by the HackMii installer. It runs homebrew from SD or USB using the apps folder layout.

compatibility.note: Installed by the HackMii installer on all three models; storage support follows the model (SD and USB, or USB only).

requirements: The HackMii installer completed successfully.
Homebrew placed in the apps folder on SD or USB.
warnings: Storage support is model-dependent: the Wii mini has no SD slot.

homebrew.name: BootMii
homebrew.summary: NAND backup and restore environment installed by the HackMii installer. BootMii-boot2 runs on every boot where the console supports it; BootMii-IOS runs from the Homebrew Channel.

compatibility.note: BootMii-IOS runs from the Homebrew Channel on any Wii Menu; BootMii-boot2 only installs on consoles with the old boot1 signing bug.
No BootMii install route is documented for the Wii Mini.

requirements: The HackMii installer completed successfully.
A supported BootMii form for the console revision.
warnings: BootMii-boot2 is not universal; do not promise it on every revision.
A NAND restore needs a usable BootMii.

homebrew.name: Priiloader
homebrew.summary: An optional pre-menu launcher that can autoboot homebrew and recover a menu that no longer starts. It is a homebrew-level recovery, not a NAND restore.

compatibility.note: wiibrew says Priiloader works on all Wiis; it installs before the system menu, not per firmware version.
No Priiloader install route is documented for the Wii Mini.

requirements: The Homebrew Channel running.
Priiloader installed before the failure it is meant to recover from.
warnings: Priiloader only works if it was installed before the failure.

homebrew.name: d2x cIOS
homebrew.firmware: Installed from the Homebrew Channel on Wii Menu 4.3; the project says not to use it on the Wii Mini.
homebrew.summary: Patched IOS installed by the guide so USB loaders work. Wrong base slots are a brick risk.

compatibility.note: Installed through the Homebrew Channel on the current Wii Menu; README describes it as a custom IOS.
README says do not use d2x cIOS on the Wii Mini.

requirements: A Wii with the Homebrew Channel installed.
The correct d2x package for the console, installed with the d2x cIOS installer.
warnings: README says do not use this on the Wii Mini.
Wrong base slots or an interrupted install can make the console unbootable; follow the project slots.
homebrew.availability: Open source; releases published by the project.

homebrew.name: USB Loader GX
homebrew.firmware: Wii Menu 4.3 with the Homebrew Channel and d2x cIOS installed.
homebrew.summary: A Wii and GameCube USB/SD loader with cover art, cheats and backup creation. It also launches other homebrew apps.

compatibility.note: Install guide requires the Homebrew Channel and d2x cIOS on Wii Menu 4.3.
Guide covers Wii and vWii; no Wii Mini support is stated.

requirements: The Homebrew Channel and d2x cIOS installed on the console.
A FAT32 USB drive or SD card for games and the loader.
warnings: Depends on d2x cIOS; without it, game loading fails.
homebrew.availability: Open source; releases published by the project.

homebrew.name: WiiFlow Lite
homebrew.firmware: Wii Menu 4.3 with the Homebrew Channel; games need d2x cIOS.
homebrew.summary: A cover-flow game and app launcher for Wii and vWii that runs titles from a USB device or SD card.

compatibility.note: README requires the Homebrew Channel or a forwarder on Wii Menu 4.3.
README covers Wii and vWii; no Wii Mini support is stated.

requirements: The Homebrew Channel or a WiiFlow forwarder installed.
A FAT32 USB drive or SD card, and d2x cIOS for game loading.
warnings: Game loading depends on d2x cIOS; no games are bundled.
homebrew.availability: Open source; releases published by the project.

homebrew.name: WiiLink Patcher
homebrew.firmware: Desktop patcher; the console side only needs a homebrew route to install the patched WADs.
homebrew.summary: Patches WiiConnect24-based channels such as Wii Room and the Photo Prints and Food channels to work with the WiiLink service. It replaces the deprecated RiiConnect24 patcher.

compatibility.note: Runs on a computer; installing the patched WADs needs homebrew on the console.

requirements: A Windows, macOS or Linux computer to run the patcher.
A Wii with a homebrew route for installing WAD files.
warnings: The older RiiConnect24 patcher is deprecated in favour of this patcher and WiiLink.
The patcher downloads channel content; it bundles no Nintendo files.
homebrew.availability: Open source; releases published by the project.
